diet.text: Mainly fish; also frogs, toads and tadpoles

overview.text: The Dice Snake is a harmless water snake of Europe and Asia. It is named after the black chequered marks on its belly, which look like the spots on dice.

identification.text: Greyish-green, brownish or almost black with dark spots on the back. The belly is often bright yellow or orange with black squares.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Much of central and eastern Europe and western and central Asia - from Italy, Germany and Czechia east to Kyrgyzstan, and from Ukraine south to Iran.

diet.text: Mostly fish, plus frogs, toads and tadpoles.

reproduction.text: Lays eggs. It sometimes hybridises with the Grass Snake and the Viperine Snake.

funfacts.text: Its chequered belly gave it its name - it looks like the spots on dice.

recognise.text: Dark spots on a grey-green or brown back.
